Professional fashion photograph, full body shot. ONE woman standing.

a fair porcelain complexion with a cool undertone, late 20s goddess, powerlifter physique THE MOST EXTREME PHYSICALLY POSSIBLE beyond all anatomy limits — an enormous, overwhelmingly powerful woman; colossal thick trapezius muscle rising high around her neck, massive round boulder shoulders, enormous thick arms with dense hard muscle, a broad powerful back, a deeply carved abdomen, colossal glutes and hips extending far beyond the shoulders, gigantic quadriceps with a deep sweep; her head looks small on top of her massive frame; not slim, not a fitness body, powerful and heavy at once; her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other, voluminous curls dark brown hair — wearing a skin-tight micro witch bodycon mini dress of ultra-thin deep purple stretch velvet with thin shoulder straps and a silver crescent-moon clasp at her throat, the front zipper pulled down the center of her chest to just above the diamond, the two sides of the stretch velvet fully covering her bust, a large diamond-shaped cutout down the center of her stomach from under her bust to her lower belly with her navel inside it, the skin inside bare, the stretch velvet remaining at her waist sides and flanks, a plain ultra-high slit cut up the right side of the dress from the hem to her hip bone, the slit baring her whole right thigh and the side of her right hip, the hem ending just below her hip bones with small silver stars sewn along it, a micro length hardly longer than a belt, her arms and legs bare, the stretch velvet shrink-wrapped onto her body like a second skin, fully opaque, her face and hands bare. Real photographic skin on her face, neck, arms, hands, stomach, thighs and legs, with visible pores and fine grain, fine peach-fuzz hairs and a faint natural flush on her cheeks and chest, a small beauty mark beside her navel and a small beauty mark near her lips. The garments cling like a second skin and show real material behaviour: the thin stretch velvet molded so closely that it shows the soft relief of her collarbones, her hip bones and the gentle rise of her bust and hips, the crescent-moon clasp, the small silver stars and the sharp clean edges of the diamond cutout, a soft velvet pile that shifts from deep purple to near black in the folds. Nails: the longest nails physically imaginable, curved talon nails each as long as her forearm is wide, in deep purple lacquer with a high polish.
Jewelry: thick polished gold bangles stacked on both wrists, heavy gold rings on every finger, and sculpted gold armbands high on both upper arms. Jewelry is metal and pearl only, worn on the body, nothing added to her face or ears.
Face: her face is bare of any garment — real living flesh with real pores, a soft sheen of natural oils and bright real catchlights, the face of a real Russian woman with high cheekbones, light eyes and a defined jaw, an unmistakably feminine face with a calm, composed expression, makeup: extremely heavy, fully saturated and bold, never subtle, faded or blended away: soft pink blush across the cheeks, sparkling pink eyeshadow, long curled lashes, large eyes with bright real catchlights, glossy candy-pink lips.

Background: a bright coastal clifftop with a grassy path, a waist-high wooden safety rail, standard-height stone steps and a white lighthouse far behind her, under a soft overcast sky with gentle diffused light, lit by natural light with soft shadows, the whole floor and surroundings clearly visible and in focus. ONE woman only. Full-length wide shot from a moderate distance with the camera at waist height, the whole figure from the soles of the boots to the top of her head completely visible, with the door, railing or steps beside her at normal human scale so the extreme heel height reads at a glance, the towering heels clearly separating the boot soles from the floor. This is one single photograph taken with one camera at one moment, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/5.6, realistic photographic grain, a real photograph.
